references.text: God reveals his name 'I am' (אֲנִי יְהוָה) to Moses, the same self-revelation repeated in 6:29.
God declares 'I am the Lord' (אֲנִי יְהוָה) to Moses, the same divine declaration as in verse 29.
God commands Moses to speak to Pharaoh everything the Lord commands him, a direct continuation of the command in 6:29.
The prophet Jeremiah receives a similar command to speak everything the Lord commands to those he is sent to.
Ezekiel is commanded to speak God's words to the people, whether they hear or not—the same prophetic mission.
God sends Ezekiel to speak his words to the house of Israel, parallel to Moses' mission to Pharaoh.
Moses is mentioned as a faithful servant who conveyed God's message, referring to his role as God's spokesperson.
The connection shows how the general command to speak to Pharaoh in 6:29 is made concrete through repeated calls for liberation throughout the plagues.
The repetition of the message 'Let my people go' in 7:26 confirms that the original command in 6:29 is a continuous and unchangeable divine plan.
The specific instruction in 9:13 illustrates how the general command in 6:29 requires concrete, time-bound obedience from the prophet.
Verse 6:13 provides the overarching context for God's specific words in 6:29 by showing that the mission includes both Moses and Aaron.
The repetition of the mission in 8:16 emphasizes that God's command in 6:29 is a continuous reality not nullified by Pharaoh's resistance.
Verse 11:1 completes the prophetic line begun in 6:29 by confirming that God's word about liberation will reach its ultimate goal.
